Let's go abroad.

The Hormuz story has actually moved — Iran now says it's agreed a deal in principle with Oman on a shipping route through the strait.

But the fine print is turning thorny: Tehran reportedly wants to bar American and Israeli ships outright, and to charge hostile countries a fee before they can pass.

That's a long way from what Washington will accept, so a signed deal is closer, but not the clean win Trump's been selling.

Meanwhile, that Gaza agreement Trump was touting last week is already in trouble.

His new Board of Peace laid out a fifteen-point plan to disarm Hamas and pull Israel back over seven or eight months, but Israel says its intelligence shows Hamas still rearming and won't move first, while fresh strikes have Hamas accusing Israel of trying to torpedo the deal.

Five days in, the two sides look further apart, not closer.

And from the science desk, one for your back.

Researchers studying zebrafish found that a faulty collagen gene lets minerals build up in the spine and fuse the discs — a lot like human disc disease.

The neat twist: an existing osteoporosis drug blocked that damage, which hints a treatment for degenerating discs and back pain might already be sitting on the shelf.

Handy science if you spend your life hanging off walls.

And your word of the day: deadpoint.

It's the controlled cousin of the dyno — you time a move so you catch the hold right at the top of your reach, the split second your body's momentum hits zero and you're weightless.

As in, "I couldn't stick that crimp on power, so I deadpointed to it instead." One AI tip while we're here: when you want a specific output format, don't describe it — show the model one or two quick examples of exactly what you want.
